scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses around calculated quarter-wave (Bragg mirror) and half-wave (defect cavity) values with ±5% perturbation will achieve higher best_target_score and maintain tightest_margin compared to uniform or random initialization, because the search begins within the resonant optical path length basin.
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to physics-aware initialization
Higher best_target_score compared to uniform 100nm starting point
Better preservation of tightest_margin across optimization rounds
known_risks: Refractive index values for ZnS and MgF2 at 4-5 μm are recalled approximations (ZnS ~2.2-2.4, MgF2 ~1.3-1.4); exact dispersion data from registry will determine actual quarter-wave thicknesses
Dual-band transmission with single defect cavity may not achieve both passbands equally; may require asymmetric mirror design or multiple defects
22 layers may not provide sufficient stopband rejection; 24 layers could improve but was not chosen to maintain comparability with prior iteration
Quarter-wave calculation uses single center wavelength (~4.4 μm) but passbands span 4.15-4.75 μm; broadband performance may differ from narrowband design
Daimon-20 substrate dispersion in mid-IR range is recalled but not verified against registry data
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase relative to iteration_04 baseline (0.5777) if physics-aware initialization improves search efficiency
valid_candidates count should remain stable or increase if initialization keeps designs within physically valid parameter space
tightest_margin should not decrease across rounds if physics-aware starting point avoids constraint violations
thicknesses_nm should show bimodal distribution clustering around quarter-wave (~480 nm for zns, ~815 nm for mgf2) and half-wave values rather than uniform 100 nm
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 10% and continue
if tightest_margin becomes negative for all candidates in a round, reinitialize with wider ±10% perturbation around physics-calculated values
